blocker: the local Recoll index covers a narrow folder set and its default AND query semantics return very small result pools, so it cannot supply the 30-50 candidate chunks this design assumes

classifier.historical_meaning: cold measurements recorded by the run that first made those calls; not this run
classifier.latency_meaning: cold network calls made in this process only; cache hits contribute none

data.ground_truth: files the session actually read or edited, matched against the retrieved pool
data.retrieval: local project-recall Recoll index via recollq

diagnosis.answer: none of them: the retrieval corpus and the sessions do not overlap
diagnosis.implication: a gate over retrieval cannot be measured until the index covers the folders the work actually happens in, which is a change to the operator's search configuration and is not taken here
diagnosis.measurement: of real sessions that worked in the CHANEL/TradeHero families, only 1 of 26 touched any file inside the folders the Recoll index covers; the sessions worked on spreadsheets, scripts and browser profiles stored elsewhere
diagnosis.question: is the fault the retriever, the pool builder, or the ground-truth matcher?

harness_failure_meaning: this is a failure of the experiment design, not evidence about Jev. The retrieval step could not produce a usable candidate pool, so no claim about a relevance gate is made in either direction.
